name: Vice-Meridian
description: Vice-Meridian is a world caught in an unrelenting geological vice, its crust squeezed between immense tidal forces that keep the interior perpetually molten. Rivers of basaltic lava carve luminous channels across the dark landscape, converging at the equatorial rift where the planetary core itself lies partially exposed, a blinding wound of white-hot metal stretching for thousands of kilometers. The sky is a permanent bruise of sulfurous yellows and deep purples, lit from below by the ceaseless volcanism.

The heat is omnipresent and oppressive, radiating from the ground in waves that distort vision even through hardened observation ports. Sulfur dioxide and carbon monoxide dominate the atmosphere, creating a toxic cocktail that would kill an unprotected human in seconds. Yet in the superheated vents along the rift, extremophilic microbial colonies flourish in rainbow-colored mats, feeding on chemical gradients that would dissolve most organic matter.

Deep scans have revealed deposits of exotic matter embedded in the partially exposed core, materials that do not conform to standard physics and whose properties shift under observation. No natural process can account for their presence, leading to speculation that Vice-Meridian's geological torment is not entirely natural, that something was placed in the core long ago, and the planet has been trying to expel it ever since.

The exotic matter alone makes Vice-Meridian one of the most valuable planets in the sector, but extraction from an exposed planetary core surrounded by lava rivers presents engineering challenges that border on the impossible. Several automated mining drones have been lost to seismic events or simple thermal failure. The matter's shifting properties suggest it may be reactive, possibly aware, and some researchers argue that attempting extraction could trigger a catastrophic response.
